codes.what_to_do: Use only the pipe's inputs and the filters the template language offers in its templates.

codes.title: An output schema was refused
codes.detail: The schema of the concept '{concept}' carries extensions or imports the runtime refuses to execute.

actor.detail: Remove the code-generation extensions and imports from the concept '{concept}', then run the method again.

other.detail: Ask the method's owner to remove the extensions from the concept '{concept}'.

concept.description: The concept whose schema was refused.

codes.meaning: An output concept's schema carries code-generation extensions or imports that the runtime refuses to execute.
codes.what_to_do: Describe the concept with the concept structure language alone, without extensions that run code.

codes.title: A dependency's content differs from its lock
codes.detail: The content of the dependency '{dependency}' differs from the hash its lock pins.

actor.detail: Check where the dependency '{dependency}' changed, then update its lock only if the change is trusted.

other.detail: Ask the method's owner to check the dependency '{dependency}'.

codes.meaning: A fetched dependency's content hashes to something other than the lock pins, so it changed since it was locked.
codes.what_to_do: Find out why the dependency's content changed, such as a moved tag. Update the lock only once the new content is trusted.

codes.title: An unexpected error occurred
codes.detail: The runtime met an unexpected error.

actor.detail: Report this to whoever runs the runtime.

other.detail: Report this to whoever runs the runtime.

codes.meaning: The catch-all: a fault of the runtime that no other code describes. It says nothing about the request, so repeating it is not advised.
codes.what_to_do: Report the problem to whoever runs the runtime, with its `pipeline_run_id` when it has one.

codes.title: The runtime is misconfigured
codes.detail: The runtime is misconfigured, so it cannot serve this request.

actor.detail: Set or correct the configuration of '{component}', then restart the runtime.

other.detail: Report this to whoever runs the runtime.

component.description: The part of the configuration that is unset or contradicts another.

codes.meaning: A setting the runtime needs is unset, or contradicts another. Nobody can wait it out: whoever runs the runtime must fix it.
codes.what_to_do: If you run the runtime, read its logs for the component, and correct its configuration. Otherwise, report the problem to whoever runs it.

codes.title: The runtime or a service it depends on is unavailable
codes.detail: The runtime, or a service it depends on, is unavailable.

actor.detail: Send the request again after a while.

other.detail: Wait, then send the request again.

codes.meaning: The runtime is overloaded or shutting down, or a service it depends on is down.
codes.what_to_do: Send the request again after `retry_after` seconds when the problem gives it.

codes.title: This runtime cannot do what was asked
codes.detail: This runtime lacks {capability}, which the request needs.

actor.detail: Enable {capability} on this runtime.

other.detail: Send a request that does not need {capability}, or use a runtime that offers it.

codes.meaning: The deployment lacks a capability the request needs, such as the asynchronous execution `/start` relies on.
codes.what_to_do: Use a route or a form of the request that this runtime offers, such as `/execute` in place of `/start`, or a runtime that offers the capability.

codes.title: The runtime could not be reached
codes.detail: The client could not connect to the runtime at {base_url}.

actor.detail: Check that the runtime at {base_url} is up and reachable, then try again.

other.detail: Try again once the runtime at {base_url} is reachable.

base_url.description: The base URL the client is configured with.

codes.meaning: The client could not open a connection to the runtime.
codes.what_to_do: Check the configured base URL, the network and whether the runtime is up, then try again.

codes.title: The runtime did not answer in time
codes.detail: The runtime did not answer within {seconds} seconds.

actor.detail: Try the call again, or raise the client's time limit.

other.detail: Try the call again.

codes.meaning: A call that creates nothing, such as a read, timed out. A call that may have created a run is `client.outcome_unknown` instead.
codes.what_to_do: Try the call again, or raise the client's time limit.

codes.title: The runtime's answer could not be read
codes.detail: The runtime answered with the HTTP status {status} and a body that is not a problem document the client can read.

actor.detail: Report this to whoever runs the runtime, with the status and the body.

other.detail: Report this to whoever runs the runtime.

status.description: The HTTP status of the answer.

codes.meaning: The answer is not a problem document, and no reading rule the client has reads it, such as an error page from a proxy in front of the runtime.
codes.what_to_do: Check what sits between the client and the runtime, such as a proxy, and report the answer to whoever runs the runtime.

codes.title: The call may have created a run
codes.detail: The connection was lost after a request that creates a run had left, so the run may exist.

actor.detail: Read the run if its id is known, and otherwise leave the outcome unknown rather than send the request again automatically.

other.detail: Read the run if its id is known, and otherwise leave the outcome unknown rather than send the request again automatically.

pipeline_run_id.description: The run, when the client learned its id before the connection was lost.

codes.meaning: The connection dropped, the call timed out, or the caller stopped it, after a request that creates a run had left, so the run may exist.
codes.what_to_do: Read the run by its id when the client knows it. A client that knows no run to read leaves the outcome unknown and never repeats the request automatically, since a repeat may start a second run.

codes.title: Following a started run stopped
codes.detail: The client stopped following the run '{pipeline_run_id}', which may still be going.

actor.detail: Read the run '{pipeline_run_id}' by its id rather than start it again.

other.detail: Read the run '{pipeline_run_id}' by its id rather than start it again.

codes.meaning: The runtime acknowledged the run, and following it then failed, so the run has started and may still be going or may have ended. The call that started it has taken effect, so it is never repeated automatically.
codes.what_to_do: Read the run by its id until it ends. Starting it again would run it twice.

codes.title: The client has no usable configuration
codes.detail: The client's setting '{setting}' is missing or unusable.

actor.detail: Set '{setting}' in the client's configuration.

other.detail: Set '{setting}' in the client's configuration.

setting.description: The setting that is missing or unusable, such as the base URL or the key.

codes.meaning: No base URL or credential is set, or the one set is unusable.
codes.what_to_do: Set the setting `params.setting` names, through the client's configuration or its environment.

codes.title: An argument was refused before sending
codes.detail: The argument '{argument}' was refused before any request left (reason: {reason}).

actor.detail: Correct the argument '{argument}', then try again.

other.detail: Correct the argument '{argument}', then try again.

codes.meaning: The client refused the arguments of a call, a command or a tool before any request left.
codes.what_to_do: Read the call's documentation for the argument and correct it.

codes.title: A local file cannot be read
codes.detail: The local file '{path}' cannot be read (reason: {reason}).

actor.detail: Check that '{path}' exists and is readable, then try again.

other.detail: Check that '{path}' exists and is readable, then try again.

codes.meaning: A local file the client was told to read cannot be read or decoded.
codes.what_to_do: Check the path, the file's permissions and its encoding, then try again.

codes.title: A local file could not be written
codes.detail: The client could not write '{path}' (reason: {reason}).

actor.detail: Make '{path}' writable, or choose another place to write, then try again.

other.detail: Make '{path}' writable, or choose another place to write, then try again.

reason.description: Why it could not be written.

codes.meaning: The client could not write a file or a directory it was asked to produce.
codes.what_to_do: Check the directory's permissions and the free space, or write somewhere else.

codes.title: The target already exists
codes.detail: '{path}' already holds something the client will not overwrite.

actor.detail: Choose another target, or remove what '{path}' holds, then try again.

other.detail: Choose another target, or remove what '{path}' holds, then try again.

codes.meaning: The target path holds something the client will not overwrite.
codes.what_to_do: Choose another target, or remove what it holds if it is no longer needed.

codes.title: Local files changed underneath the client
codes.detail: Another process holds or changed '{path}', which this call read.

actor.detail: Try again once the other process is done with '{path}'.

other.detail: Try again once the other process is done with '{path}'.

codes.meaning: Another process holds the lock on, or wrote, the files the call read.
codes.what_to_do: Wait for the other process to finish, then try again.

codes.title: An output does not match the generated types
codes.detail: The output field '{field}' does not match the generated type of the concept '{concept}'.

actor.detail: Generate the types again from the method as it is now.

other.detail: Generate the types again from the method as it is now.

concept.description: The concept whose generated type refuses it.

codes.meaning: The caller's generated types refuse an output that the method declares, usually because the method changed after they were generated.
codes.what_to_do: Generate the types again from the current method.

codes.title: A download link was refused
codes.detail: The client refused a download link the runtime's storage handed out (reason: {reason}).

actor.detail: Make the runtime's storage hand out https links that need no redirect.

other.detail: Report this to whoever runs the runtime.

reason.description: Why the link was refused: it is plain http, it uses another scheme, or it redirects.

codes.meaning: The client's fetch policy refused a link that the runtime's storage handed out.
codes.what_to_do: If you run the runtime, configure its storage to hand out https links. Otherwise, report the problem to whoever runs it.

codes.title: A download passed the client's limit
codes.detail: A download passed the client's limit of {limit} bytes.

actor.detail: Raise the client's download limit, or download fewer files at once.

other.detail: Raise the client's download limit, or download fewer files at once.

codes.meaning: A file, or the call's total, passed the client's own download cap.
codes.what_to_do: Raise the limit in the client's configuration, or download the files one at a time.

codes.title: The call was stopped by the caller
codes.detail: The caller stopped the call before it finished, and the call created nothing.

actor.detail: Make the call again if its result is still wanted.

other.detail: Make the call again if its result is still wanted.

codes.meaning: The caller's abort signal stopped a call before it finished, where the call creates nothing, such as a read, or its request had not left yet. A call that creates a run and was stopped after its request left may have created the run, so it is `client.outcome_unknown` instead.
codes.what_to_do: Make the call again if its result is still wanted.

codes.title: A local tool the client needs is missing
codes.detail: The program '{tool}', which the client needs, is missing or cannot be started.

actor.detail: Install '{tool}' and put it on the PATH, then try again.

other.detail: Install '{tool}' and put it on the PATH, then try again.

codes.meaning: A program the client needs, such as a runtime's command-line tool, git or uv, is missing, cannot be started, or failed to install.
codes.what_to_do: Install the program, check that it is on the PATH, and try again.

codes.title: A local tool is too old
codes.detail: The program '{tool}' is at version {version}, older than the client requires.

actor.detail: Upgrade '{tool}', then try again.

other.detail: Upgrade '{tool}', then try again.

codes.meaning: A program or an engine the client needs is older than it requires.
codes.what_to_do: Upgrade the program to the version the client documents, and try again.
